summary: Thursday titles pass for How Tech Works: 16 of the 19 reference videos at 500K+ views state their title ('How X Works') while all 8 of ours ask a question, so a statement-title challenger is now on the weekly loop's list. I also added the feed's first AI topic: what a chatbot does to write one word.
why: Statement titles have a median of 4.6M views against 2.1M for question titles among the references, and our question titles come from a rule built on money Shorts. The Shorts feed had no AI topic although AI is a core lane in the profile, and the new topic scores 8.91 (the feed's lowest is 7.34).

findings.title: Reference titles state, ours ask
findings.detail: 16 of 19 references at 500K+ views use a statement ('How Electrical Outlets Work' 77.3M, 'How Starlink Actually Works' 4.6M); the week's top on-profile breakout is 'NVIDIA's First Chip' (1.78M on 29.8K subscribers). All 8 of our Shorts use a question title.

findings.title: No AI topic in the Shorts feed
findings.detail: The how-AI and how-internet formats are long-only, so tonight's AI topic is told as a zoom_inside Short. Its reference has 1.02M views on 12.7K subscribers (80.6x).

findings.title: Facts for the chatbot topic
findings.detail: OpenAI: a token is about 4 characters, and 100 tokens are about 75 words. Meta: Llama 3 has a 128K-token vocabulary and a 70B model. Kaplan 2020: about 2 operations per parameter per token. Code computes about 140 billion operations per token.

findings.title: Claude Code 2.1.332
findings.detail: Routines are renamed 'cloud scheduled tasks' in the UI, skills can come from MCP servers (beta), and headless Agent calls are no longer reported finished too early. No action needed.
